text: The desert spat secrets when it felt like it. Today it gave up a ridge of brick half-buried in sand. A windstorm had stripped the dunes down to hard earth and left the upper edge exposed. Zik crouched at the dig and brushed grit from the mortar with his fingers. The bricks were ordinary baked clay, worn down by time. The mortar wasn't. In places it had turned glassy and black, the kind of change that only came from heat no ordinary fire could make. The joints sat too clean. Too exact. His father's voice returned with the clarity of something said the day before.
